attacks.claim: The Recent signers template renders the full name and the postal code, contradicting the agreed rule (first name, last initial, city only) and the proposal's own description. This exposes personal data of EU and US signers publicly.

The marketing opt-in checkbox is pre-checked and its wording bundles 'others from the organizer'. Under GDPR, consent must be an unambiguous affirmative act, specific and granular. This also contradicts the 'optional... signers can choose' claim. The organizer CSV export then distributes these invalid consents to third parties.

Errors are conveyed only by border and background color on invalid fields, with no text message. The aria-live region is never populated by the JS and no aria-invalid is set. The form has novalidate, so screen reader users get no error feedback. This violates WCAG 2.1 AA (1.4.1, 3.3.1, 3.3.3). The axe scan cannot detect this.
attacks.evidence: for (const name of fields) form.elements[name].classList.add('is-invalid'); ...

attacks.claim: The client JS has no handling for non-422 failures such as 409 duplicate, 429, or 5xx, and no catch for network errors. The user sees nothing on failure. A 409 on duplicate would silently do nothing, and the rollout watches sign_submit_error_rate.
attacks.evidence: if (res.status === 422) {...} if (res.ok) window.location = ...; // no other branch

attacks.claim: QA does not cover the privacy and a11y acceptance criteria, which is how the template deviations went unnoticed. The test table lacks a check of the public panel format, a manual screen reader/keyboard pass, or a GDPR consent check. The only a11y evidence is an automated scan, which covers a limited subset of WCAG.
attacks.evidence: Recent signers renders 20 most recent confirmed | Pass; axe-core automated scan on sign page | 0 violations

attacks.claim: Duplicate detection by exact email can be bypassed via case or plus-address variants, so counts could be inflated. The proposal gives no normalization.
